newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK business confidence high despite 1997 - poll.
newsitem.headline: HK business confidence high despite 1997 - poll.

text.p: An overwhelming majority of Hong Kong's American Chamber of Commerce members expressed "favourable" view of the colony's business environment over the next five years, the business group's survey said on Wednesday.
The British colony will revert to China at midnight on June 30, next year. Concerns have been raised whether the favourable investment atmosphere in Hong Kong would continue after the handover.
More than 95 percent of 633 respondents said they were positive about Hong Kong's business environment in the next five years, which was an increase from last year's 91 percent, the poll said.

"Survey results confirm that Hong Kong will remain the region's commercial hub and preferred site for the location of regional headquarters for AmCham members," the local chapter of American Chamber of Commerce said in a statement.
The poll found 99 percent of respondents planned to retain business operations in Hong Kong.
More than half of the respondents, 53 percent, said they planned to expand operations, while 42 percent said they expected to conduct business as usual, it said.
The survey also found 99 percent of companies expected their performance over the next three years either to be good or satisfactory.
Of the 488 respondents that currently have a presence in China, 86 percent planned to increase their investments over the course of the next three years, it said.
